G2-57's asserted clause requires every terminal state of chat_sessions.status to hold a contact method. Of the two terminal states, lead_captured holds one by construction (ChatCaptureAction creates a ChatLead with a NOT NULL phone before the status write) and escalated held none. ChatEscalateAction::handle now refuses a session with no ChatLead, returning capture_required with refusal_code NO_CONTACT_METHOD_ON_SESSION, leaving the session non-terminal and dispatching no ChatEscalated, per GOAIEZ-MASTER-PLAN.md:25618 (the thread never dead-ends). Refused: a contact_method column on chat_sessions (a derived column whose only writer exists to satisfy its reader), reusing offline_form (which means AI credits exhausted), and an exhaustive walk over the old behaviour (which would have asserted the plan's own forbidden outcome). --ruling R245

ChatCaptureAction::handle now refuses a blank or whitespace-only phone before any write, throwing DomainException NO_CONTACT_METHOD_ON_CAPTURE, so neither the Person nor the ChatLead is created. This is the input half of SITE-151's terminal-state invariant: that guard is an existence check on ChatLead, and chat_leads.phone is NOT NULL but not non-empty, so a blank phone would have produced a lead the guard admits and a session reaching escalated with no way to reach anyone, which is GOAIEZ-MASTER-PLAN.md:29073's forbidden outcome. It also closes a second consequence of the same input: Person::updateOrCreate keys on business_id and phone, so two blank-phone captures for one business collapsed onto one Person. The predicate is trim() === '', matching the decision already recorded for the email field at ChatCaptureAction:29-30 (R245, 2026-09-05); email stays optional and becomes null, phone is required and is refused. Refused: making chat_leads.phone nullable, adding a non-empty clause to ChatEscalateAction's guard instead of or as well as this refusal (a reader compensating for a writer, and two writers of one invariant), and widening the refusal to email. --ruling R245

FormCaptureAction's spam branch keyed its Person on ['phone'] ?? '+15550000000', and the null-coalescing operator fires only on a missing key, never on a blank value. Two consequences, both already decided against in the same file's non-spam branch at line 93 (R245, 2026-09-05): a payload carrying an empty or whitespace-only phone keyed a Person on the empty string, so two blank-phone spam submissions from one business collapsed onto one contact; and a payload with no phone key wrote the reserved fictional number +15550000000 to a production contact row. The spam branch now takes its phone through the same given() normaliser the non-spam branch uses and gives a phone-less spam submission its own contact. The keying changed and nothing else: a spam rejection is still stored and flagged with a non-null person_id, per G3-64 and G13-05 at GOAIEZ-MASTER-PLAN.md:31363. Refused: adding a refusal in the shape of X-102's ChatCaptureAction, which would discard a spam submission and delete a discharged capability; making persons.phone non-nullable; and narrowing X155Test.php:1133, whose assertion is correct but whose fixture reaches only the non-spam branch. --ruling R245

The published page omits a schema node whose validator-required strings are blank, rather than emitting it or substituting a label, because SchemaRenderAction refuses the whole document on an empty name and the JSON-LD block is one of J11 seven required elements (R245)

--ruling R245 The reddened X157Test assertion that a malformed video block takes the whole JSON-LD off the served page asserted the behaviour SITE-154 changed, not a contract. The guard field lists are byte-identical to SchemaRenderAction validateSchema required-non-empty lists, and the fixture block carries no contentUrl, so it is exactly the member the guard excludes. The test now asserts that the required JSON-LD element survives and that the malformed video does not reach it. The whole-document refusal is preserved and still asserted for the case where it is correct, a blank top-level business name, at X176Test line 290.

A top-level schema name or url that is blank after trim now refuses the whole document, as the empty string already did. empty() returns false for a whitespace-only string, so a business whose name was whitespace published a LocalBusiness node carrying a blank name with the document intact and every gate green, while the empty-string case was refused and that refusal is asserted at X176Test line 290. The direction is deliberately opposite to the collection-member seam: a blank enrichment member is omitted and the document survives, but the top-level name is the subject of the whole schema, so the document is refused. The member predicates are unchanged, because two committed falsifiers depend on the validator accepting a whitespace member in order to show that member reaching the page with the page intact. Refused: a guard in EdgeDeployAction as well as or instead of this one, and a non-empty constraint on businesses.name, which is another lane column.

--ruling R245 X-176 — The top-level required-string check no longer refuses a name or url of "0". SITE-156 gave the line below it a trim-based blank test that already refuses a missing key, null, a non-string and any blank-after-trim value, which left the older empty() check with exactly one live effect: refusing the non-blank string "0", a legitimate name that schema.org validates. G7-48 asks for a refusal only when the schema does not validate, so a business named 0 was serving six of the seven required elements. @type deliberately keeps empty(), because isset on an empty array is true and validType computes 0 === 0 for it, so a uniform rewrite would have admitted an empty @type array. Refused: any change to the member predicates, on which two committed falsifiers depend; to EdgeDeployAction completeness guard, whose blank-name gap is governed by G7-48 requiring the page to render without the schema; and to businesses.name, another lane column.

The blank test for a display string on the publish path is now trim-based at all five sites, replacing empty(), which was wrong in both directions over a NOT NULL pages.title column with no non-empty validation. A page legitimately titled 0 was treated as untitled and removed itself and its whole subtree from the published nav and breadcrumb, while a whitespace title was treated as present and rendered an anchor with no visible text. The nav and the breadcrumb are two renderers of one hierarchy, so both were changed together with the identical predicate and one test asserts they agree; changing one alone rebuilds a divergence that appears in no diff of either file. Refused: a non-empty constraint on pages.title, whose only writer has zero production callers so no reader can rely on it; isset, which is always true over a NOT NULL column and would make the guard dead while appearing fixed; and relaxing any test that reddens.

--ruling R245 The honeypot presence check no longer uses empty(), which treated a bot writing the string 0 into the hidden field as having left it blank, so the guard did not fire, FormSpamRejected was never dispatched, and FormCaptureAction took the legitimate branch and stored the submission as a real Person and a real lead. G3-64 and G13-05 require that a spam rejection is stored and flagged, never discarded, so a submission that is not recognised as spam at all defeats the clause. The predicate is now present, not null, not the empty string and not an empty array, which is the same emptiness set the Laravel prohibited rule uses at StoreFeedbackRequest line 73, where a comment already records the intended semantics: a human never sees the field and a bot filling every input does. Refused deliberately: a trim based test, which is correct for a display string such as a page title but wrong here, because a honeypot is a presence signal and whitespace in it is something having been written, so trimming would let that bot through a case empty() already catches. The remedy for a blank test is decided by what the value means and is not uniform across the sites one grep returns. Two tests assert the two directions and each is reddened by a different mutation, so the wrong remedy is refused by the suite and not only by a note.
